newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian ex-premier says FLN leaders out of favour.
newsitem.headline: Algerian ex-premier says FLN leaders out of favour.

text.p: Algeria's former premier Mouloud Hamrouche, a leading figure in the former ruling Liberation National Front (FLN), said his party leadership had lost credibility and warned of a grass-roots revolt to bring it down.

"The current leadership has no representation any more. It represents nothing and it is unable to continue to repesent the FLN and speak on its behalf," said Hamrouche in interview published on Wednesday in the Algerian newspaper al Khabar.

Hamrouche, prime minister from 1989 to June 1991, was among several party figures who signed a statement this week lambasting the FLN leadership for its policy seen as too close to President Liamine Zeroual's government ahead of general elections within the next eight months.
FLN chief Boualem Benhamouda convened on Wednesday the party central policy-making committee to decide party strategy before a general election promised for next year.
The FLN ruled Algeria for 29 years, from independence to reforms in 1991. It is now in opposition.
Cancellation of Algeria's first multi-party general election in January 1992 provoked a bloody power struggle with Moslem fundamentalists whose party had taken a leading position in the election.
FLN insiders said the internal struggle was pitting what they called the reform wing, including Hamrouche, against the "conservative" leadership over holding a party congress soon.
They said the top leadership wanted to delay any congress, arguing that the time was not ripe, while their adversaries reckoned the leaders feared being ejected by the membership at the congress.

"From our point of view, the central committee meeting is pointless because, whatever decisions emerge from the meeting, it will change nothing as the leadership is disconnected from the party base," said Hamrouche who along with other senior party officials is boycotting the central committeee meeting.
